classification.difficultyReason: Select parallel-line angle relationships and combine supplementary angles or angles at a point.

content.prompt: This question reviews angles across transversals. Find the angles marked with pronumerals, giving reasons.

spec.description: Two parallel oblique lines crossed by a steeper transversal; matching single arrows and all six point labels retained.
spec.mathematics: AB parallel CD; 140 degrees at G and alpha at F are alternate interior angles.
spec.answerVisibility: Only supplied angle and unknown are visible.

answer.worked:
$$\alpha=140^\circ$$
Alternate angles are equal because $AB\parallel CD$.

spec.description: Two oblique parallels with single arrows and two vertical parallels with double arrows.
spec.mathematics: AB parallel CD and PQ parallel RS; 65 degrees, beta and gamma occupy corresponding upper-right sectors.
spec.answerVisibility: Only 65 degrees, beta and gamma are shown.

answer.worked:
$$\beta=65^\circ$$
Corresponding angles are equal because $AB\parallel CD$.

$$\gamma=\beta=65^\circ$$
Corresponding angles are equal because $PQ\parallel RS$.

spec.description: Open chain VWXYZ with two distinct parallel-mark families.
spec.mathematics: VW parallel XY; WX parallel YZ; angle VWX is 100 degrees.

answer.worked:
$$\begin{align*}\alpha+100^\circ&=180^\circ\\\alpha&=80^\circ\end{align*}$$
Co-interior angles are supplementary because $WV\parallel XY$.

$$\beta=\alpha=80^\circ$$
Alternate angles are equal because $WX\parallel YZ$.

spec.description: Quadrilateral NKLM with both pairs of opposite sides marked parallel.
spec.mathematics: NK parallel ML, NM parallel KL; interior angle L is 68 degrees.
spec.answerVisibility: Alpha, beta and gamma are unknown interior angles.

answer.worked:
$$\begin{align*}\beta+68^\circ&=180^\circ\\\beta&=112^\circ\end{align*}$$
Co-interior angles, $NK\parallel ML$.

$$\begin{align*}\alpha+\beta&=180^\circ\\\alpha+112^\circ&=180^\circ\\\alpha&=68^\circ\end{align*}$$
Co-interior angles, $NM\parallel KL$.

$$\begin{align*}\gamma+68^\circ&=180^\circ\\\gamma&=112^\circ\end{align*}$$
Co-interior angles, $NM\parallel KL$.

spec.description: Two oblique parallels with one transversal and co-interior labels.
spec.mathematics: AB parallel CD; theta and 2theta are co-interior angles.

answer.worked:
Co-interior angles are supplementary because $AB\parallel CD$.

$$\begin{align*}\theta+2\theta&=180^\circ\\3\theta&=180^\circ\\\theta&=60^\circ\end{align*}$$

spec.description: Three parallel segments AD, BE and CF, joined by DE and EF.
spec.mathematics: Angle ADE is 50 degrees; angle CFE is 35 degrees; theta is the right-facing angle DEF.

answer.worked:
$$\angle BED=180^\circ-50^\circ=130^\circ$$
Co-interior angles, $AD\parallel BE$.

$$\angle BEF=180^\circ-35^\circ=145^\circ$$
Co-interior angles, $BE\parallel CF$.

$$\begin{align*}\theta+130^\circ+145^\circ&=360^\circ\\\theta&=85^\circ\end{align*}$$
Angles at a point sum to $360^\circ$.
